analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | 11.2.26 11.6.26 Weekend Edition
key_insights: Industrials fell 280bps on the week, slightly underperforming broader markets. Materials outperformed but still fell 150bps.
Sharp unwinds under the surface: builders rose over 400bps while technology fell almost 500bps.
Smaller cap, highly levered consumer names squeezed: JBLU +30%, DFH +27%, GPK +26%. Straggler earnings also did well: VNT +16%, SWK +12%.
Data center related names fell most: STRL, ECG and LGN down to -27%, FPS, MOD and VRT off 22%. Poor earnings sent OEC down 26% and KMT down 21%.
Next week starts conference season for Q4 commentary and early 2027 views. Investor days: RPM, ENTG, WCC, WOR, KBR, MGA. Late earnings focus on FERG and TDG.

The desk sees opportunities as much less thematic and more idiosyncratic. It cites elections, AI/data center capital raises, US rates vs rest of world, dollar and inflation expectations, and geopolitical turmoil as the moving pieces.

GS Prime: US equities were modestly net sold on the week (-0.4 SDs vs 1-year), driven by the largest single stock net selling in 4+ months. Macro Products (index and ETF) were net bought for a second straight week (+1.5 SDs), with long buys to short covers about 3 to 1.
US-listed ETF shorts rose 7% on Thursday Nov 5, the largest 1-day increase since March and 3rd largest in 5 years. They rose 3.3% week/week, led by shorting in Large Cap Equity ETFs.

Single stocks saw the largest net selling in more than 4 months (-2.1 SDs), with long sales to short sales at 3.8 to 1. Info Tech, Industrials, Staples and Health Care were the most net sold sectors. Utilities, Real Estate and Financials were the most net bought.

US Industrials were the most net sold sector (-3.3 SDs, long and short sales ~2 to 1). The % net selling was the largest since Apr 2020 and second largest on record (since 2016). Nearly all subsectors were net sold except Machinery and Airlines, led by Electrical Equip, Building Products, Trading Companies & Distributors, Aerospace & Defense and Ground Transportation.
US Industrials long/short ratio is 1.61, the lowest since Jan 2024 and in the 3rd percentile of 5-year history.

FERG reports pre-market with a 7% implied move and was up after three of the last four reports. Short interest is 7mm shares vs 1.5mm earlier this year, which the desk attributes to residential exposure. Valuation is 20x EPS and 14x EV/EBITDA, at the high end of its historical range. Top holders have been net buyers.

TDG reports fiscal Q4 pre-market with a 6% implied move and was down after six of the last eight reports. Short interest is flat at about 1mm shares (3 days to cover, 2% of shares). Valuation is at the lower bound. Consensus expects FY27 EPS growth to accelerate to 19% from 11% while revenue growth slows to 12% from 19%.

TDG: reports fiscal Q4 pre-market (call 10am), implied move 6%, down after six of the last eight reports. Consensus estimate (not reported) for FY27 EPS growth is 19% vs 11%, and for revenue growth is 12% vs 19%.
OEC fell 26% and KMT fell 21% on the week after poor earnings results. VNT rose 16% and SWK rose 12% after straggler earnings.
